title: An optimized intracerebroventricular injection of CD4+ T cells into mice
protocol: Anesthetize the mouse in the induction chamber filled with 2% isoflurane.
Confirm sufficient anesthesia by assessing the foot-pinch response.
Clean the head area with a cotton tipped applicator soaked in 70% ethanol, avoiding the eye area.
Make a vertical incision down the center of the head starting between the eyes using a scalpel.
Use a cotton tipped applicator to expose the skull and dry the area.
Place the mouse in the stereotaxic apparatus, positioning the nose in the anesthesia adaptor with a constant flow of 2% isoflurane.
Tighten the ear bar on the right-hand-side until the head is firmly in place.
Set the position of the left-hand-side ear bar at the start of all injections.
Place the mouse over the heating pad to prevent hypothermia during the procedure.
Lubricate the mouse's eyes with Viscotears Liquid Gel to prevent corneal dryness.
Insert the drill into the holder of the stereotaxic apparatus.
Gently place the tip of the drill at the bregma position.
Set the dorsoventral axis to zero mm on the stereotaxic apparatus.
Raise the tip of the drill and move directly down to the Lambda position.
Lower the tip of the drill to the skull.
Adjust the head position if the dorsoventral axis is not ≤ 0.1 mm.
Repeat the alignment until bregma and lambda are on the same horizontal plane.
Ensure the head is in the correct position and stable for accurate ventricular injections.
Drill two small holes in the skull just large enough for the needle to pass through and infiltrate the brain surface.
Follow the coordinates measured from the bregma: −0.5 mm in the anteroposterior axis, ±1 mm in the mediolateral axis, and −2.3 mm in the dorsoventral axis.
Be careful not to cause brain damage during drilling.
Optimize the dorsoventral coordinate for your specific mice prior to experiments as it might change depending on the mouse strain and age.
Inject cells into the lateral ventricles through the drilled holes.
Add 1 mL of PBS to a previously prepared aliquot of cells.
Centrifuge at 500 g for 5 min at 20°C.
Remove the supernatant and suspend in 2.5 μL PBS.
Load the Hamilton syringe with the desired treatment (transduced CD4+ GFP T cells suspended in PBS) or control (PBS or control cells suspended in PBS).
Ensure there are no air bubbles in the syringe.
Position the syringe over the first hole, lower the needle until it is touching the brain, and set the dorsoventral axis to zero mm.
Very slowly lower the needle to −2.3 mm in the dorsoventral axis.
Set the infusion pump to administer the injection at a rate of 1 μL per minute.
Once the infusion is finished, wait for 2 min before raising the needle slowly to −1.15 mm in the dorsoventral axis.
Wait 1 min before slowly raising the needle out of the hole.
Always wait the recommended time before raising the needle and raise the needle slowly to minimize backflow.
Repeat the same procedure for the second lateral ventricle.
Close the incision using a stainless steel wound clip.
Sacrifice the mouse 72 h post injection.
Perfuse the mouse with 10 mL cold PBS.
Harvest the brain.
Suspend the brain in 4% paraformaldehyde for 48 h at 4°C.
Switch to 30% sucrose in PBS solution for 48 h, or until the brain has sunk to the bottom of the tube.
Embed the brain in O.C.T. compound and freeze blocks at -20°C.
Cut brains into 40 μm sections using a microtome.
Rinse tissues in 0.5% Triton in PBS solution for 30 min.
Rinse tissue twice with PBST for 5 min.
Transfer the tissues to DAPI 1:3000 in PBS and incubate for 5 min.
Rinse the tissues with PBST for 5 min.
Transfer the tissue onto a slide.
Add anti-fade fluorescence mounting medium and cover the sections with a cover slip.
Image brain sections on a FLUOVIEW FV1000 laser-scanning confocal microscope.
